newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada House panel suggests no drug patent change.
newsitem.headline: Canada House panel suggests no drug patent change.

text.p: A parliamentary committee recommended on Thursday that Canada maintain the 20-year period under which drugs would maintain patent protection, but suggested moving toward national pharmacare.

"The committee believes that Canada should remain committed to our international trade obligations. The committee accepts the 20-year patent period," the House of Commons Standing Committee on Industry said in a report.
Some had recommended cutting the period to enable medical costs to be reduced.
But the committee also suggested the government should look at paying Canadians' drug costs.
"Because pharmaceutical products are medically necessary, the committee believes steps should be taken to investigate the feasibility of a national pharmacare program," it said.
"While the overwhelming majority of Canadians are presently covered by some form of public or private insurance, we must recognize the needs of those who are not."
